mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate consistently signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a strong labor market driving consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of UNRATE decline and RSAFS increase does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market slowdown (HOUST below 1050 thousand units), consumer confidence and spending weaken, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in the late-cycle expansion regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1050 during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate and slowing job growth (PAYEMS) indicates a tightening monetary policy coinciding with a cooling labor market, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of FEDFUNDS rise and PAYEMS decline does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
